meta.title: Cybersecurity Services — SOC, CIRT & SIM3 Audits | Tech4TIME

core.title: The Capability We Build
core.lead: Most providers sell you tooling. We build the function itself — the team, the process and the platform — and then measure it against an international standard so you can prove it works.

items.title: Building a Full Comprehensive SOC & CIRT
items.text: A Security Operations Centre and Computer Incident Response Team stood up end to end: threat landscape assessment, gap analysis, secure architecture, implementation, and the reactive and proactive maintenance that keeps both running afterwards.

items.title: Conducting SIM3 Audits
items.text: SIM3 is the maturity model CSIRTs are assessed against worldwide, scoring organisation, human, tool and process parameters. We audit an existing team against it, report where it stands, and set out what closing each gap takes.

note.text: Both run on our OSSF framework — eight stages from measuring the threat landscape through to business continuity.

items.name: IT Equipment Supply
items.schema_description: Multi-vendor hardware sourcing and licensing, deployment and imaging, lifecycle support, secure erasure and responsible disposal.

meta.title: IT Equipment Supply — Sourcing, Deployment & Disposal | Tech4TIME
meta.description: Multi-vendor hardware sourcing, configure-to-order builds, on-site deployment, lifecycle support, secure data erasure and responsible disposal from Tech4TIME.

core.title: The Capability We Build
core.lead: Twenty-two services covering the whole life of a hardware estate — from the first quotation through to the disposal certificate.

items.title: Vendor-Neutral by Default
items.text: We buy across competing vendors rather than reselling one of them, so the specification answers to your requirement instead of to a distribution agreement. That applies to laptops and servers the same as it does to switches, firewalls and the licences that run on them.

items.title: Owned From Purchase Order to Disposal Certificate
items.text: Sourcing is the easy part. We image and configure before delivery, install and cable on site, tag every unit into an asset register, carry the warranty and RMA chasing, plan the refresh — and when it is finally retired, erase the media and recycle it through a licensed route.

note.text: Every group below is drawn from the capability list we publish on the services page.

layers.title: Sourcing, Deployment, Lifecycle, Security and Disposal
layers.lead: Twenty-two services across five groups. Everything below is on the page whether or not scripting is available — the tabs only choose which group is in view.

items.title: Procurement & Sourcing
items.tab_text: Buying the right equipment at the right price
items.text: Hardware and licensing bought across competing vendors rather than resold from one, so the specification answers to the requirement instead of to a distribution agreement.

cards.name: Multi-Vendor Hardware Sourcing (Laptops, Desktops, Servers)
cards.desc: Laptops, desktops, workstations and servers sourced across competing vendors rather than resold from a single brand.
cards.purpose: Let the specification follow the requirement, and keep pricing honest by putting suppliers against one another.

cards.name: Custom Configuration Services (Configure-to-Order)
cards.desc: Machines built to an agreed specification — processor, memory, storage, peripherals — before they ever ship.
cards.purpose: Arrive with hardware that already matches the role it was bought for, instead of upgrading it after delivery.

cards.name: Software Licensing & Package Supply
cards.desc: Operating system, productivity and specialist licences supplied alongside the hardware they will run on.
cards.purpose: Keep licence counts, renewal dates and entitlement in one place rather than scattered across departments.

cards.name: Bulk Procurement & Volume Discounting
cards.desc: A rollout consolidated into a single order so unit price falls as quantity rises.
cards.purpose: Cut the total cost of a large deployment without splitting it across suppliers and warranty terms.

cards.name: Enterprise Networking Gear (Routers, Switches, Firewalls)
cards.desc: Routers, switches, firewalls and the optics and cabling that join them, specified against the network design.
cards.purpose: Supply network hardware sized for the topology it will actually carry, not for the catalogue it came from.

items.title: Deployment & Implementation
items.tab_text: Getting it installed, configured and recorded
items.text: The work between a delivery of boxes and working infrastructure: imaging, installation, cabling, and an asset record that exists from day one rather than being reconstructed later.

cards.name: Pre-delivery Imaging & Configuration
cards.desc: A standard image, security baseline and application set applied to every unit before it leaves us.
cards.purpose: Deliver machines that are usable on day one instead of consuming a week of desk-side setup.

cards.name: On-site Installation & Physical Setup
cards.desc: Racking, mounting, powering and connecting equipment in place, at your premises.
cards.purpose: Turn a delivery into working infrastructure without pulling your own team off their work.

cards.name: Asset Tagging & Inventory Recording
cards.desc: Every unit tagged, serialised and recorded against its location, its owner and its warranty state.
cards.purpose: Know what you own, where it is and when it falls out of support — before an auditor asks.

cards.name: Network Infrastructure Setup & Cabling
cards.desc: Structured cabling, patching, switch configuration and the physical network layout behind them.
cards.purpose: Give the site a cable plant and a switching layer that can be extended rather than rebuilt.

cards.name: Peripheral Integration (Printers, Scanners, UPS)
cards.desc: Printers, scanners, uninterruptible power supplies and the rest of the equipment around the desk.
cards.purpose: Bring peripherals onto the network and into monitoring rather than leaving them as unmanaged islands.

items.title: Lifecycle & Support Services
items.tab_text: Keeping it working, and planning what replaces it
items.text: Support for equipment already in service — repair, warranty, monitoring — and a dated view of when each class of hardware reaches the end of its useful life.

cards.name: Hardware Maintenance & Repair Services
cards.desc: Diagnosis, parts and repair for equipment in service, whether or not it is still inside its warranty.
cards.purpose: Keep working hardware working, so one fault does not force an early refresh of everything around it.

cards.name: Warranty & RMA Management
cards.desc: Warranty claims and return authorisations pursued with the vendor on your behalf, start to finish.
cards.purpose: Take the chasing off your team, and make sure entitlement is used before it quietly lapses.

cards.name: Proactive System Monitoring
cards.desc: Health, capacity and error telemetry watched across the equipment we supply and support.
cards.purpose: Catch a failing disk or an overheating unit while it is still a maintenance job rather than an outage.

cards.name: Leasing & Rental Solutions
cards.desc: Equipment supplied on a lease or a short-term rental instead of an outright purchase.
cards.purpose: Move hardware from capital to operating expenditure, or cover a project that does not justify buying.

cards.name: Technology Refresh Roadmapping
cards.desc: A dated plan for when each class of equipment reaches end of life and what is due to replace it.
cards.purpose: Spread replacement cost across budget years instead of meeting it all at once when things start failing.

items.title: Security & Compliance
items.tab_text: Hardware that answers to your security obligations
items.text: The security side of an equipment estate: machines specified for it, media destroyed properly when they leave, and a register that can answer an audit.

cards.name: Cybersecurity-focused Hardware Provisioning (TPM, Biometrics)
cards.desc: Machines specified with a Trusted Platform Module, biometric authentication and firmware protections enabled.
cards.purpose: Put disk encryption and strong local authentication on a hardware footing rather than a policy one.

cards.name: Secure Data Erasure & Storage Media Destruction
cards.desc: Verified wiping of storage media, and physical destruction where wiping alone is not sufficient.
cards.purpose: Make sure equipment leaving your estate carries no recoverable data, with documentation to show for it.

cards.name: IT Asset Management (ITAM) Reporting
cards.desc: A maintained record of every asset, its licences, its owner and its position in the lifecycle.
cards.purpose: Answer ownership, licensing and disposal questions from one register instead of a spreadsheet hunt.

cards.name: Compliance-ready Backup & Disaster Recovery Hardware
cards.desc: Backup appliances, offline media and recovery hardware sized against the retention rules you have to meet.
cards.purpose: Hold the recovery capability your obligations assume, not just the capacity that happened to be spare.

items.title: Sustainability & Disposal
items.tab_text: Retiring an estate without leaving a mess
items.text: What happens at the end: recycling through licensed routes, recovering residual value from what still has some, and specifying the next estate to draw less power than the last.

cards.name: E-Waste Recycling & Responsible Disposal
cards.desc: Retired equipment routed through licensed recyclers rather than to landfill or an unregulated reseller.
cards.purpose: Retire hardware in a way that stands up to an environmental audit and does not leak your data on the way out.

cards.name: Hardware Buy-back & Trade-in Programs
cards.desc: Residual value recovered from equipment you are retiring and offset against whatever replaces it.
cards.purpose: Turn an end-of-life estate into part of the budget for the next one rather than a disposal cost.

cards.name: Energy-efficient Infrastructure Consulting
cards.desc: Advice on specification, consolidation and cooling that lowers what the estate draws from the wall.
cards.purpose: Cut running cost and heat output, which is often the real constraint in an existing server room.

core.title: The Capability We Build

items.title: Advice That Survives Your Budget
items.text: Strategy, enterprise architecture and virtual CIO or CTO advisory, costed in terms a finance function will accept. We would rather tell you a workload should not move, or that buying beats building, than sell you the larger engagement and be right about neither.

items.title: Capability You Keep
items.text: Training in the stacks we build on ourselves, taught by the engineers who use them — plus the awareness, adoption and service-management training that decides whether a rollout lands. The point is that your own people can run it after we leave.

layers.title: Advisory, Technical Skills and Delivery
layers.lead: Twenty-eight services across five groups. Everything below is on the page whether or not scripting is available — the tabs only choose which group is in view.

items.title: Strategic & Advisory Consultancy
items.tab_text: Where the technology is going, and why
items.text: Board-level work: what the estate should look like in three years, what it costs to get there, and which decisions have to be taken in what order.

cards.name: Digital Transformation Roadmapping
cards.desc: An assessment of where the organisation is now, a target it can credibly reach, and the phases between them.
cards.purpose: Replace a wish list with a sequence, so each phase pays for or de-risks the one that follows it.

cards.name: IT Strategy & Business Alignment
cards.desc: Technology plans built from what the business is trying to do rather than from what the technology can do.
cards.purpose: Stop IT spend and business priorities drifting apart until neither side trusts the other’s numbers.

cards.name: Enterprise Architecture Design
cards.desc: A structured view of systems, data and integration that new work has to fit into.
cards.purpose: Keep each project from solving its own problem in a way that creates three for everybody else.

cards.name: Virtual CIO/CTO Advisory
cards.desc: Senior technology leadership on a fractional basis, for organisations that need the judgement but not the salary.
cards.purpose: Get the seniority to challenge vendors, own the roadmap and report to the board without a full-time hire.

cards.name: IT Budgeting & ROI Planning
cards.desc: Total cost of ownership modelled across the life of a decision, not just its purchase price.
cards.purpose: Make the case for spend in terms a finance function will accept, and know when a project stops paying back.

cards.name: Cloud Readiness & Migration Strategy
cards.desc: An honest assessment of which workloads should move, which should not, and in what order.
cards.purpose: Avoid the two usual failures: migrating everything because it is fashionable, or nothing because it is hard.

items.title: Technical & Specialized Consultancy
items.tab_text: Deep work on one specific problem
items.text: Engagements scoped around a single question — how exposed are we, should we build or buy, will we actually recover — answered with evidence rather than opinion.

cards.name: Cybersecurity Risk & Vulnerability Assessments
cards.desc: A measured view of exposure across the estate, with findings ranked by what they would actually cost you.
cards.purpose: Direct limited security budget at the risks that matter instead of the ones that scan most loudly.

cards.name: Data Analytics & Business Intelligence Strategy
cards.desc: How data is modelled, where it lives and which numbers the organisation agrees to run on.
cards.purpose: Get one version of each figure, so meetings argue about the decision rather than about the spreadsheet.

cards.name: Software Selection & “Build vs. Buy” Analysis
cards.desc: A requirements matrix, a shortlist and a cost comparison across building it and buying it.
cards.purpose: Make the choice on evidence, and know the switching cost before the contract rather than after it.

cards.name: DevOps & Infrastructure Optimization
cards.desc: A review of how work actually reaches production, and where it stalls on the way.
cards.purpose: Shorten the distance between a commit and a release without lowering the bar it has to clear.

cards.name: Disaster Recovery & Business Continuity Planning
cards.desc: Recovery time and recovery point objectives agreed with the business, then a plan built to meet them.
cards.purpose: Find out whether the plan works during a rehearsal rather than during an incident.

cards.name: Compliance & Regulatory Auditing
cards.desc: Current practice mapped against the obligations that apply, with the gaps written down.
cards.purpose: Walk into an audit knowing what will be found, and having already started closing it.

items.title: Technical Skills Training
items.tab_text: Engineering skills, taught by engineers who use them
items.text: Training in the stacks we build on ourselves — the same frameworks, platforms and tooling our delivery teams work in every day.

cards.name: Software & Application Development (Next.js, Golang Gin Framework, PostgreSQL)
cards.desc: Application development in the stack we build on ourselves, from framework fundamentals to database design.
cards.purpose: Give your developers working competence in the tools your own systems are written in.

cards.name: Cloud Platform Training (OpenStack)
cards.desc: Operating and administering an OpenStack private cloud, taught against a real deployment rather than slides.
cards.purpose: Leave your team able to run the platform themselves rather than depending on whoever built it.

cards.name: Network & Infrastructure Administration (Cisco, CompTIA)
cards.desc: Routing, switching and infrastructure administration along the Cisco and CompTIA syllabuses.
cards.purpose: Build the baseline competence an infrastructure team needs, and prepare candidates for the exams.

cards.name: Cybersecurity & Ethical Hacking
cards.desc: Offensive technique taught defensively — how intrusions actually work, practised in a contained lab.
cards.purpose: Understand an attack well enough to detect and stop it, not just to recognise its name.

cards.name: AI & Machine Learning Implementation
cards.desc: Taking a model from a notebook to something that runs, is monitored and can be retrained.
cards.purpose: Move past experiments to machine learning that is actually in production and maintained.

cards.name: Data Science & Advanced Analytics
cards.desc: Statistical method, feature work and the visual presentation of a result someone has to act on.
cards.purpose: Produce analysis that holds up to scrutiny and is understood by the people who commissioned it.

items.title: User & Operational Training
items.tab_text: Everyone else who has to use the systems
items.text: The training that decides whether a rollout lands: awareness, everyday tooling, onboarding onto new systems, and the service frameworks around them.

cards.name: Security Awareness & Phishing Simulation
cards.desc: Awareness training reinforced with simulated phishing, measured over time rather than run once.
cards.purpose: Move the click rate, which is the only awareness number that means anything.

cards.name: Productivity Suite Mastery (Microsoft 365, Google Workspace)
cards.desc: Practical competence in the everyday suite, including the collaboration features most people never find.
cards.purpose: Recover the hours lost to doing manually what the tools already do, and to duplicated documents.

cards.name: New System Onboarding & Adoption
cards.desc: Structured onboarding for a newly introduced system, with adoption tracked after go-live.
cards.purpose: Stop a good system failing because nobody was shown how it fits their actual job.

cards.name: IT Service Management (ITSM) Frameworks (ITIL, Agile)
cards.desc: Service management practice along ITIL and Agile lines, applied to how your teams already work.
cards.purpose: Give support and delivery a shared vocabulary and a process that survives the people who wrote it.

cards.name: Proprietary Software/ERP User Training
cards.desc: Role-based training on an ERP or in-house system, built around what each role actually does in it.
cards.purpose: Train people on their own workflow rather than on a generic tour of every module.

items.title: Training Delivery Models
items.tab_text: How the training is actually run
items.text: The same material delivered in whichever shape fits — a workshop on site, a portal people work through at their own pace, or one-to-one time with an executive.

cards.name: Bespoke In-House Workshops
cards.desc: Sessions run at your site on a curriculum written against your systems and your constraints.
cards.purpose: Train a team together on the environment they will go back to, using their own examples.

cards.name: On-Demand E-Learning Portals
cards.desc: Material people work through at their own pace, with progress visible to whoever owns the programme.
cards.purpose: Cover shift workers, distributed teams and new joiners without rerunning the same session forever.

cards.name: One-to-One Executive Coaching
cards.desc: Private sessions for senior staff who need the substance without sitting in a room with their own team.
cards.purpose: Let leadership ask the basic questions candidly, which most will not do in front of the people they manage.

cards.name: Intensive Bootcamp Sessions
cards.desc: Multi-day immersion, heavy on hands-on lab work and assessed at the end.
cards.purpose: Take a group from little exposure to working competence inside a defined block of time.

cards.name: Certification Preparation Programs
cards.desc: Preparation mapped to a published exam blueprint, with practice testing and a study plan.
cards.purpose: Get candidates through the exam first time, rather than paying for the retake.
